items.title: Round 1: 15 architecture questions
items.description: The interview page asked what the default loop is, what "task" means, who owns entity kinds, where DNA lives, and how drift is stopped. You answered all 15: 9 with a pick, 6 with notes asking for more thought.

items.title: The loop starts and applies your picks
items.description: "task" now means a task packet only, and the positional prompt fills the words input (about 20 flows migrated). A first-run worker prints a clear "trust this folder once" message. Gates that had no verdict stopped picking a branch by position. Your 03:48 sync committed these.

items.title: Research on your open notes, then round 2
items.description: 6 research lanes (eval before the task, validation pickup, entity kinds, loop variants, DRY vs drift, the DNA map) plus a critic. The result was the round-2 page with 40 follow-up calls, and a census of all 43 core packages with 14 questions.

items.title: Gates that could never fail
items.description: Two enforced gates were passing against a package that no longer exists, and a runtime guard named 2 deleted test files; both fixed. A census found 214 flow steps in 56 flows that nothing runs, so they go to the model as "Execute shell command". Measured: rejecting unknown steps breaks 0 tests.

items.title: Programs, triggers and CLI routing
items.description: Registration now refuses programs whose flow cannot run (committed in your 12:18 sync). Only 4 of 85 registered programs have ever fired for real. 164 of 296 declared CLI commands do not route, including the pre-push session capture, which has never worked. The first 4 decisions were written up.

items.title: Decisions 2, 5, 1, 6, 7 and 8 prepared
items.description: Each got a Fable 5.1 advice seat, a held patch, a failing-then-passing test and a check that it applies. Startup slowness (27-60 s per lev call) was profiled: slow disk reads made worse by the tsx cache, not a code regression.

items.title: Vault bug, and the first combined check
items.description: Secrets written by lev vault could not be read by a second process because the key salt was never saved; two held patches fix it (7 failing tests before, 41 passing after). Applied together, the 11 patches passed every recipe check except one registry-name clash, which got two alternative fixes.

items.title: Combined check v2, and Fable ranks the decisions
items.description: 18 patches applied together in a fresh worktree: every recipe check passed, and a real lev vault store/get worked across processes. Fable agreed with 7 of the recommendations and proposed the ruling order.

items.title: Decision 9: which export a command runs
items.description: Three resolvers pick a handler three ways. A new registry check found 40 of 139 registered commands that cannot resolve. Fixes for discourse-graph (6), the index refresh duplicate and pricing. 26 CLI commands silently ignore their flags; 8 were confirmed live. Combined check v3: all 23 patches stack.

items.title: Your rulings
items.description: 9 decisions, then apply the held patches in order and run their recipe checks.

props.content: Your notes are paraphrased here; the verbatim text is in `~/.local/state/lev/spikes/arch-burndown-20260927/interview-answers/raw-20260927.json`. "Built" means code landed and was tested; "round 2" means the question went to research and came back as follow-up calls you have not answered yet.

rows.q: When `lev exec` runs, which loop is the default?
rows.a: One rule: is there a task to check against?
rows.then: Built: a task run without a flow uses the shipped sdlc flow; a bare prompt says "Nothing was verified".

rows.q: What should the default verify step check?
rows.a: Note: check spec-compliance fields, not only the prompt; model the eval before the task starts, because agents pad validation with made-up scripts.
rows.then: Research lane "eval before the task" → round 2.

rows.q: Which worker does a fresh project get?
rows.a: Keep tmux claude-code and print a clear "trust this folder once" message.

rows.q: What does "task" mean on the command line?
rows.a: A task packet only; your words go to another input that the positional prompt fills.

rows.q: What makes a flow a conforming work loop?
rows.a: Check the graph shape, for task runs and flows that opt in.
rows.then: Built as a check: 92 of 141 graphs fail it once bound to a task.

rows.q: How does a domain plugin extend the core loop?
rows.a: The domain ships a whole flow that passes the loop check; evaluator packs fill its verify gate.

rows.q: What is DNA from now on?
rows.a: Note: DNA needs decomposing; define the Lev IR and its ontologies first.

rows.q: How do rules reach the plan and act prompts?
rows.a: Code selects the rules from the slice's allowed paths and shows them as "done when" statements. Note: verification needs a deep dive after entities, verbs and DNA.

rows.q: When verify fails, clean up or start over?
rows.a: Clean up by default. Note: support every variant so you can test which works best; plan/act/verify are words for explaining, not variable names.
rows.then: Now a standing loop rule: every variant selectable.

rows.q: Should entity kinds be declared by folder?
rows.a: Note: the same conventions as today; file-based routing preferred, config YAML is fine too.

rows.q: Who owns each kind?
rows.a: Core owns the work kinds and sdlc extends them. Note: put decision in the workstream too; sdlc may own spec and ADR (to debate); everything needs strong types.

rows.q: Three faces of one task: markdown compiled to YAML?
rows.a: Note: not realistic; status can be updated mechanically; maybe one md and one yaml; views go to generative UI in Jarvis.

rows.q: Which command does a skill call after writing an entity?
rows.a: Note: this was meant to be picked up per module, convention over config, so agents cannot pass arbitrary checks.

rows.q: Where do lifecycle skills and templates ship from?
rows.a: Split by owner. Note: how has eval builder drifted? Maybe a new Lev with the new pieces, rather than changing skills that work.

rows.q: Copied facts: one owner and a check everywhere?
rows.a: Note: stop canonizing, this is context; research agent-managed code bases; show sequence diagrams of how "never copy a fact" would actually work.

props.label: YOUR ANSWERS
props.title: The 15 questions you answered, and what happened to each
Success reported for work nothing did
props.content: Flow steps that no runner handles go to the model as "Execute shell command: <op>": 214 steps in 56 flows. Flows with such steps finish green with nothing run. `--flowmind-program` and `--flowmind-file` run nothing but label the run as if they did. Printing help counts as success. Decisions 1, 5 and 8.
props.label: FALSE GREENS

props.title: Gates that could not fail
props.content: Two enforced gates were passing against a package that no longer exists. A runtime guard named 2 deleted test files. A gate with no verdict picked its first branch. All fixed; the gate fixes were committed in your 03:48 sync.
props.label: GATES

props.title: Declared CLI commands that do not route
props.content: 164 of 296 declared commands fail or run something else. The git pre-push session capture has never worked (0 captured events since 2026-04-11). `lev status` is still unimplemented; that was already ruled in the n1 decision. Decision 2.
props.label: CLI ROUTING

props.title: Programs that never fire
props.content: 88 programs declared; 76 register, 9 are refused, and 3 declared in core never load. Only 3 both load and get real triggers. One program re-triggered itself (1789 failures, already fixed on 09-23). Decisions 3 and 7.
props.label: PROGRAMS

props.title: Vault secrets could not be read back
props.content: The key salt was random and never saved, so a second process could not decrypt what the first stored. Two held patches: save the salt in a header, then read CLI arguments with the secret on stdin only. The real vault was never touched.
props.label: VAULT

props.title: Three ways to pick a command's handler
props.content: The SDK path, the CLI path and the command list each resolve a handler differently. 40 of 139 registered commands cannot resolve at all. The registry check has a list of known broken commands that may only shrink; fixes for discourse-graph (6) and index refresh have landed as held patches. Decision 9.
props.label: HANDLERS

props.title: CLI flags silently ignored
props.content: 26 CLI commands expect an object and drop CLI flags; 8 were confirmed live (graph-query, graph-get-entity, graph-traverse, graph-trace-lineage, graph-find-similar, graph-infer, oauth-status, oauth-doctor). `lev pricing --provider=exa` answered with model prices; its patch is held. Root cause: arguments declared in a `handlers:` config section that nothing reads.
props.label: INPUT

props.title: The environment fought back
props.content: `lev` calls took 27-60 s because of slow directory reads made worse by the tsx cache. The code-graph tool is stuck on 2026-09-16 lock files. A worktree `dist` symlink wrote stale flows into main's catalog; the catalog was rebuilt and a memory note added.
props.label: ENVIRONMENT
WHAT WE FOUND
props.title: Eight patterns behind most of the findings

props.content: Each decision in the record has its evidence with file and line references, the options with why-not, advice where it was sought, and what it holds. Recommendations are the loop's, checked against Fable 5.1 where noted; none is a ruling until you make it.

rows.q: 1. A flow step no runner recognises is handed to the model. Fail instead?
rows.opts: a fail closed everywhere now · b fail at run time now, report first, enforce after migration · c keep the model fallback behind a setting

rows.q: 2. 164 of 296 declared CLI commands do not route
rows.opts: a fix routing in core/poly · b delete unused declarations, wire the live ones · c report-only check first
rows.prep: step 1 (capture-push + 5 vault verbs) + name fix B (A is the alternative)

rows.q: 3. Programs that never fire or cannot run
rows.opts: a per-plugin pass · b registration warning only · c bulk unregister
rows.prep: cheap cut (2 never-written entries) + lock-test roster

rows.q: 4. The trustgraph backend is named in DNA, but core never imports plugins
rows.opts: a the plugin registers its adapter · b allowlist the import in the boundary gate · c move backend selection out of context-graph
rows.rec: a (Fable: a canon conflict to rule first) (medium)

rows.q: 5. A command result with no success field: success or failure?
rows.opts: a align the outlier (only success:false fails) · b fail closed everywhere · c a now, b as a ratchet
rows.rec: a (divergence kept: the loop leaned c) (medium)

rows.q: 6. `lev exec --profile` has never announced the profile
rows.opts: a delete the event and its trigger · b apply the prepared listener · c listener, validate phase only

rows.q: 7. Programs declared in core configs never load
rows.opts: a scan core too · b core declares no programs · c leave them, report them

rows.q: 8. `--flowmind-program` and `--flowmind-file` run nothing
rows.opts: a delete both flags (use --flow) · b make them run · c stop the false success first

rows.q: 9. Three resolvers disagree on which export a command runs
rows.opts: a one shared resolver · b narrow to #export else handler (withdrawn) · c document the three · d (refuted) · e keep the SDK rule; CLI fails closed until decision 2

The loop committed nothing itself. Three of your sync commits included its work:

- **`4797228d1` (03:29):** the round-1 gate fix in core/eval and core/flowmind.
- **`512d6806f` (03:48):** gates that fail closed in core/exec, "task" means a task packet, and the trust-this-folder message.
- **`27f06bfbf` (12:18):** programs whose flow cannot run are refused at registration; exec tests write a real task packet; the cdo boundary audit runs its 5 commands; the earlier flow fixes (rust-plan, exec-validate, deepen-plan, 4 sdlc steps); the pre-push hook logs capture output; two sdlc tests stop writing into the real event log.

These went in with syncs, not reviewed commits, so their commit messages do not carry the tested/not-tested notes. The test counts are in the handoff for each tick.

props.title: Five things the loop could not do

props.content:
- **Move the unread `handlers:` config sections into `poly.sdk`** (context-graph, imessage, sentinel; 23 commands with arguments). context-graph's `query` clashes with code-graph's `query`, and 9 handler files answer to two CLI names. Tied to decision 2.
- **sdlc ralph trigger:** its registered command is the missing trigger for the dormant ralph flow; fold into decision 3's per-plugin pass.
- **qit-engines SDK:** compile, validate and g_tower from `schemas/engine.schema.yaml`; there is live intent in `dna/vernacular.yaml` and core/world-model.
- **Triggers for 62 programs with no emitter** (decision 3).
- **Per-module CLI cleanup:** 43 unimplemented, 27 shadowed and 71 unknown surfaces (decision 2).
- **Who owns the spec lifecycle** (decision 3).

Earlier ticks also logged: verification beyond schema checks (your answer on rules), the blast radius of rejecting unknown steps (measured: 0 tests break), and an acyclic-trigger gate.

props.label: DEEP DIVES
props.title: Six potential tasks the loop logged instead of doing

props.content:
**Rules:** no commits; no git stash, checkout or reset; typecheck plus named test files only; potential tasks go to the sweep ledger; every loop variant stays selectable; everything saved to disk each tick so nothing lived only in the conversation.

**Advice:** Fable 5.1 answered 17 questions. Each answer was saved verbatim and checked against the code before it was used. Where Fable and the loop disagreed, both positions were kept, not blended.

**Mistakes caught and corrected:**
- Tick times written between 04:35 and 06:05 were guesses, running up to 2 hours ahead. They were caught against file timestamps, corrected, and a memory note was added: run `date` before stamping.
- The handler census first counted any default export as a match, which hid 14 broken commands. It now follows re-exports and was re-proven live.
- The loop's own recommendation for decision 9 was withdrawn when it turned out to cross a DNA safety gate.
- Five claims from Fable were refuted and recorded, for example "27 affected entries" (it was 12).
- The tick-65 probe first compared a wrapped result, so its verdicts were wrong. It was fixed and rerun before anything was recorded.
- This page's check found the "waiting for commit OK" list was stale: your 12:18 sync had committed it. Both records now say so.
